subject: RFI: model source attribution, licensing implications & pinning attestation
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@globex.com>

Cc: Globex RFP <rfp@globex.com>

Subject: RFI: Model catalog - source attribution & version controls

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for participating in Globex's model catalog RFI. A few clarification items came up from our security and legal teams around open-model licensing, provenance records, and how Redwood pins/rolls updates to served models. Please could you provide a concise write-up addressing the following by EOD Oct 6 so we can include it with our vendor evaluation materials: 

- How does Redwood record and surface the source/origin for models in your catalog (commit-level provenance, license file capture, SBOMs)?
- When a model in your catalog is updated upstream (license changes, security fixes), what is your change-control and notification process for customers using pinned versions?
- For customers that require cryptographic evidence of a particular snapshot, can Redwood provide hash manifests or signed attestations?
- Any constraints on redistribution or derivative use for models served through Redwood we should be aware of (commercial redistribution, attribution requirements)?

Attached is the supplemental questionnaire from procurement. Let me know if you prefer a short call instead; we have a 30-minute slot open Oct 7 at 10:00 AM ET.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Sr. Manager, AI Procurement
Globex Corporation

Subject: Re: RFI: Model catalog - source attribution & version controls

Alicia —

Thanks for the clear list. Please find our consolidated response attached (PDF) and summarized below. I'm copying Marissa (solutions) and Kimberly (legal/compliance) for any addenda. If helpful we'll also produce a signed attestation template and a sample audit extract.

Summary answers (high-level):

1) Provenance & catalog metadata
- For every model we onboard, we capture: source repo or upstream artifact URL, upstream commit/hash (when available), license file text and SPDX identifier (automatically parsed), and a generated SBOM that lists model artifacts and associated weights. These fields are surfaced in the model catalog UI and API under "Origin" and "Provenance".
- Evidence artifacts (commit diff, license snapshot, SBOM) can be exported as a downloadable ZIP via the Console or fetched through the catalog API.

2) Pinning, change control, and notifications
- Customers may pin to a specific catalog snapshot (model ID + snapshot hash). Once pinned, we treat that snapshot as immutable for that customer.
- Upstream updates create a new catalog snapshot but never mutate pinned snapshots. We notify customers via console notification and registered webhook + email when a new snapshot is available. Notification timelines: 30 days for non-security upstream changes, ASAP for security patches (include severity and CVE references).

3) Cryptographic attestations and manifests
- We can provide SHA256 manifests for any catalog snapshot and sign them with a Redwood KMS-backed signing key upon request. We also offer an attestation template (editable) that we can sign and return as a PDF or DocuSign envelope for procurement.

4) Licensing and redistribution constraints
- We do not relicense upstream models. Redistribution or derivative obligations stem from the upstream model license. Our catalog surfaces license obligations prominently and flags models with incompatible licenses for commercial redistribution.
- For open-models with attribution-only clauses, we capture the required attribution strings and include them in the model metadata and generated attribution README.

Deliverables attached: Redwood_RFI_Model_Catalog_Response_v1.pdf (consolidated answers), and a link to our provenance playbook.

Next steps
- If Globex wants signed hash attestations for pinned snapshots we will: (a) generate a signed SHA256 manifest, (b) produce an attestation using the attached template, (c) record the transaction in our audit log and export CSV sample. Please confirm which snapshots you'd like us to attest.
- We're available for the Oct 7 10:00 AM ET slot — I'll hold that for now.

Thanks,

Aditya —

Thanks for the quick reply and the summary. A few follow-ups from legal and security: 

- When you say "we do not relicense upstream models" — can you confirm whether models hosted via Redwood can be downloaded by customers and redistributed, or whether commercial redistribution must follow upstream license terms only? Any additional indemnity language in your T&Cs would be helpful to highlight.

- For the attestation workflow: does the signed manifest include a Redwood signature and timestamp that is verifiable independently (i.e., public key or certificate chain we can validate)?

- For pin rollback: if a pinned snapshot is discovered to have a critical vulnerability after pinning, do you offer remediation assistance (e.g., backporting fixes, recommended mitigations) or only notification and suggested upgrade paths? And do you keep an immutable copy of the original snapshot for audit?

Also, can you provide an anonymized sample of the audit log CSV export to show the fields we would receive (timestamp, actor, action, snapshot_hash, comment)? That will help our SOC team triage.

Appreciate it — if easiest we can confirm during the Oct 7 call.

Best,
Alicia

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@globex.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-06T16:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Model catalog - source attribution & version controls

Alicia —

Answers below, inline, and attached a couple artifacts (attestation template and anonymized audit CSV sample). I've included the exact steps we follow so your security team can map them to controls.

> "When you say 'we do not relicense upstream models' — can you confirm whether models hosted via Redwood can be downloaded by customers and redistributed?"
- Clarification: Redwood does not relicense or alter upstream license terms. Customers with catalog access may be able to export model artifacts depending on the deployment mode and contract: 
  - Hosted API: model weights are not exported by default — API access is offered under our platform terms; downstream redistribution is governed by upstream license and by contract.
  - Dedicated / Private deployments: customers can control export permissions operationally; in Private deployments the customer typically manages the artifacts and thus redistribution is governed by their contract and the upstream license.
- For procurement: we'll flag export-capable deployment options in the commercial SOW and include language that clarifies redistribution liabilities. Kimberly will follow up with a redline excerpt of the relevant clause.

> "Does the signed manifest include a Redwood signature and timestamp that is verifiable independently?"
- Yes. We produce a SHA256 manifest for the snapshot and sign it with our KMS-backed RSA key. Verification steps: (1) fetch manifest, (2) fetch Redwood public signing key via our JWKS endpoint, (3) validate signature and timestamp. We can provide a pre-generated public key or certificate chain to Globex's PKI team if you prefer out-of-band verification.

> "For pin rollback and remediation assistance"
- Immutable copies: every pinned snapshot is stored immutably for audit purposes and kept for the life of the customer's retention window (default 18 months; configurable).
- Remediation assistance: for Critical/High vulnerabilities we offer: 
  1) Immediate notification and rollback guidance.
  2) If the issue is upstream and a patched snapshot is available, we can perform a canary rollout to the customer's non-production routes and support validation testing.
  3) For Dedicated/Private customers we can coordinate backporting or provide recommended mitigations and, where contractually scoped, assist with a backport. Backport support is an options add-on in our enterprise services.

> "Anonymized sample of the audit log CSV export"
- Attached: Catalog_Audit_Log_Sample.csv (columns: timestamp, actor_email, action, resource_type, resource_id, snapshot_hash, comment, request_id).

Action items we will take now:
- Kimberly will produce a redline of the commercial clause around export/redistribution and share within 48 hours.
- We will sign and return an attestation for any snapshot you designate; please send the snapshot_hash(es) you want attested.
- I'll also upload a short (2-page) technical note describing the JWKS verification flow for signatures to the shared Drive link.

If you want the attestation executed as a DocuSign envelope we can do that as well. Confirm your preference and which snapshots to attestate and we'll start the work.

Thanks again — looking forward to the call on Oct 7.
